question: What is the main study of pharmacology?

options.A: The legal distribution of controlled substances in hospitals
options.B: How chemical substances interact with living systems
options.C: Surgical techniques used alongside medicinal treatments
options.D: The commercial manufacturing and packaging of herbal remedies

explanation: You've got this! Pharmacology simply looks at how drugs and chemicals affect living bodies.

question: How is toxicology different from standard pharmacology?

options.A: Toxicology focuses specifically on harmful effects and poisons
options.B: Toxicology deals exclusively with the retail pricing of drugs
options.C: Toxicology only studies medications derived from synthetic chemicals
options.D: Toxicology examines how plant roots are crushed for remedies

explanation: Great job! While pharmacology studies all drug actions, toxicology zooms in strictly on poisons and harmful reactions.

question: What does pharmacokinetics mean?

options.A: What the body does to the drug over time
options.B: How chemical structures are built in a laboratory
options.C: What the drug does to change cellular function
options.D: How nurses calculate pediatric dosages safely

explanation: Think of pharmacokinetics as your body's journey with the drug—absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion!

question: A patient has severe liver disease. Which part of drug processing will most likely be affected?
explanation: Spot on! The liver is our main metabolic factory where drugs are broken down and processed.

question: Which drug name is given by the manufacturer and always starts with a capital letter?
explanation: Brand names (like Panadol) are created by companies for marketing and are always capitalized, unlike generic names.

question: Why is it super important for nurses to know the generic name of a drug?

options.A: It is the only name recognized by hospital billing departments
options.B: It remains universal and prevents confusion across different manufacturing companies
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact physical shape and color of the pill
options.D: It automatically guarantees the drug is more affordable for the patient

explanation: You nailed it. Generic names stay the same everywhere, saving us from company name confusion!

question: Where does the heart medication digoxin originally come from?
explanation: Fun fact! Digoxin is a classic heart medicine originally extracted from the purple foxglove plant.

question: What is the main benefit of grouping drugs by their therapeutic use?

options.A: It groups medications that treat similar medical conditions together
options.B: It dictates the exact manufacturing cost of the chemical compound
options.C: It proves which brand name version of the drug is superior
options.D: It eliminates the need for any pharmacokinetic testing in humans

explanation: Exactly! Therapeutic classification helps us easily see which drugs treat which illnesses.

question: Which route delivers medication straight into the bloodstream, bypassing the digestive system?
explanation: Right into the vein! IV administration means the drug goes straight into circulation immediately.

question: An emergency patient needs medicine right now. Which route will work the fastest?
explanation: You got it! IV is the champion for speed during emergencies because it enters the blood instantly.

question: What do we call a strange, unexpected drug reaction that happens because of a patient's unique genetics?
explanation: Idiosyncratic means it's a rare, one-of-a-kind reaction that catches everyone by surprise based on body chemistry.

question: What is the primary goal of pharmacovigilance in healthcare?

options.A: To monitor and detect adverse drug reactions to ensure patient safety
options.B: To calculate the wholesale manufacturing cost of generic drugs
options.C: To supervise the physical packaging of pills in pharmacies
options.D: To market new pharmaceutical products to international hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Pharmacovigilance is all about watching out for bad drug reactions to keep patients safe.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the safety rules for giving medications?
explanation: Haha, room decor won't help your patient! We stick to the vital rights like right patient, drug, dose, route, and time.

question: You are about to give a blood pressure pill, but your patient's blood pressure is already dangerously low. What is your best first step?

options.A: Ask a family member to double-check the hospital chart
options.B: Administer the drug anyway since it was already ordered
options.C: Hold the medication and notify the prescribing doctor
options.D: Crush the pill to speed up its absorption in the stomach

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! Always assess your patient first—if the drug could cause harm, hold it and call the doctor.
